Type-to-speak engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Live Speech capability covers storefront language. Xcode, entitlements, and Connect actually separate text-to-speech in the app from product-page copy:

  • Text-to-speech pipelines & voice synthesis — in-app code that converts typed text to spoken audio via AVSpeechSynthesizer, Personal Voice, or custom TTS. Controls voice quality and latency. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • Personal Voice training & voice selection UI — engineering work for voice onboarding, phrase boards, and speak-aloud controls. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains type-to-speak value to buyers.
  • On-device vs cloud synthesis — your binary may synthesize speech locally, require network access, or both. Listing copy should match what screenshots actually show — not promise offline 实时朗读 when your gallery only shows cloud TTS.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of type-to-speak in the app.

Working type-to-speak flows in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other. Live Speech listing copy is not Dictation, Live Caption, VoiceOver, or Speak Screen

Accessibility and speech apps blur several surfaces indie teams conflate. AppLocale covers listing metadata only — type-to-speak and Live Speech marketing on the product page:

  • Live Speech & type-to-speak (this page) — Live Speech, type-to-speak, speak typed text aloud, Personal Voice with Live Speech, 实时语音, 实时朗读, 键入朗读, 输入即朗读, phrase boards, and description copy about typing and speaking aloud in conversations.
  • Dictation & voice typing (different) — Dictate text, Speech-to-text keyboard, Voice typing, keyboard voice input. See Dictation listing guide — turning speech into typed text is the opposite direction from Live Speech.
  • Live Caption & real-time subtitles (different) — live captions, real-time subtitles, 实时字幕 for media, calls, or spoken audio playback. See Live Caption listing guide — captions display spoken audio as text; Live Speech speaks typed text aloud.
  • VoiceOver & screen reader (different) — VoiceOver support, Works with VoiceOver, screen reader accessibility badges. See VoiceOver listing guide — not type-to-speak communication copy.
  • Speak Screen & Spoken Content (different) — system features that read on-screen content aloud to the user. Not the same as a user typing a custom phrase and speaking it in a conversation — do not reuse Speak Screen vocabulary for Live Speech screenshots.

Your screenshots may show multiple surfaces in one gallery. Listing copy should name the correct one per frame — a type-to-speak keyboard is not a Live Caption subtitle bar, not a dictation mic button, not a VoiceOver badge, and not a Speak Screen toggle unless that is what the frame shows.

Live Speech-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Type-to-speak marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Live Speech workflows — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Live Speech vs generic text-to-speech

US pages use "Live Speech", "Type to speak", or "Speak typed text aloud." China storefront copy often uses 实时语音, 实时朗读, 键入朗读, or 输入即朗读 — depending on whether you mean Apple's Accessibility feature name, conversation type-to-speak, or general speak-aloud UX. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual type-to-speak scope, not inventing Personal Voice support your app does not ship.

Personal Voice vs system voices

Screenshot galleries may label Personal Voice (个人声音) separately from generic TTS voices. Buyers searching for communication-accessibility apps distinguish on-device voice cloning from standard speech synthesis — match what your English listing and screenshots actually show.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need type-to-speak search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 实时语音, 键入朗读, and 个人声音 each signal different intent from generic accessibility keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Type to speak" headlines on gallery frames — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

Promotional text refreshes

Live Speech feature launches and Personal Voice milestone updates often land in the 170-character promotional text field above the description — updatable without a new binary. See Promotional text in Simplified Chinese when your type-to-speak pitch lives in promo text rather than the long description.

Why machine-translated Live Speech copy fails

  • Literal "Live Speech" → awkward 现场演讲 (public speaking sense) instead of commerce-idiomatic 实时语音 or 键入朗读
  • Generic "Speak typed text" → 朗读输入的文字 (correct but stiff) instead of buyer-friendly 输入即朗读
  • English badge headlines preserved on zh-Hans screenshots — "Type to speak" with no Chinese benefit line beside it
  • Overlay text overflow — long English Live Speech captions pasted into short screenshot callout zones truncate on device
  • Conflating 实时语音 with 语音识别 — buyers searching for type-to-speak may not match speech-recognition keywords meant for dictation apps
  • Conflating 实时朗读 with 实时字幕 — Live Speech speaks typed text; Live Caption shows subtitles for heard audio — different buyer intent
  • Inconsistent vocabulary between listing description, promotional text, and screenshot captions when all three mention Live Speech

Machine translation is fine for internal drafts. Finished Live Speech strings need idiomatic zh-Hans that states what type-to-speak workflows you ship — while keeping accurate scope. AppLocale rewrites by hand; we do not deliver raw Google Translate or LLM output as finished copy.
